  224: where the sum runs over all irreducible representations of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. $D_K$ is block-diagonal in this decomposition (this is the block-diagonal theorem from Session 22b, verified to $8.4 \times 10^{-15}$). Each block contributes eigenvalues $\{\lambda_{(p,q),n}\}$ with multiplicity $d_{(p,q)}^2 = (1 + p)(1 + q)(1 + \frac{p+q}{2})^2$.
  225: 
  226: These are the normal modes of the phononic crystal. Each mode is a standing wave because $K$ is compact: the eigenfunction $\psi_{(p,q),n}$ oscillates (has nodes and antinodes) on $K$ but does not propagate. Its time evolution is $e^{-i\lambda_{(p,q),n} t}\psi_{(p,q),n}$ -- pure oscillation, no translation.
  227: 
  228: ### 7.2 The Ground State as the Filled Dirac Sea

  230: The ground state of the phononic crystal is the filled Dirac sea: all negative-energy modes occupied, all positive-energy modes empty. By the spectral pairing theorem (T3: $\{\gamma_9, D\} = 0$), for every eigenvalue $\lambda$ there exists $-\lambda$.
